item.title: (1965) Rubber Soul
item.description: Listen to McCartney’s bass on “Drive My Car”: it is no longer the root-note thump of the Merseybeat records but a melodic line, syncopated and insistent, pushing against the vocal with the rhythmic independence that James Jamerson of The Funk Brothers had been perfecting on Motown singles since 196...

item.title: (1965) "California Girls"
item.description: The introduction has nothing to do with California, or girls, or the beach.

item.title: (1966) "Reach Out, I'll Be There"
item.description: A solo piccolo opens the record, high and keening over a galloping percussion figure, and for a few seconds “Reach Out, I’ll Be There” sounds less like a Motown single than like the title music to a film that has not started yet.

item.title: (1966) "You Can't Hurry Love"
item.description: James Jamerson’s bass enters bouncing and syncopated, weaving against Benny Benjamin’s drums, and for the next two minutes and forty-five seconds everything else in the arrangement orbits that figure.

item.title: (1967) "Strawberry Fields Forever", "Penny Lane"
item.description: A Mellotron set to its flute voice plays four bars of something that sounds like a barrel organ heard underwater, and one of the strangest, most ambitious double A-sides in pop arrives.

item.title: Bernard Herrmann
item.description: Alfred Hitchcock wanted the shower scene in Psycho to play in silence.

item.title: Curtis Mayfield
item.description: The sound that made Curtis Mayfield unmistakable was built from a child’s shortcut.

item.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto
item.description: As a Tokyo high schooler, Ryuichi Sakamoto rode a packed commuter train twenty minutes every morning and started counting the noise.

item.title: PLACES
item.description: The rooms, corners, and addresses of New York where the MAP’s history happened.

item.title: Brian Eno
item.description: On Roxy Music’s first two records there is an instrument the credits can’t quite name: the rest of the band, fed through Brian Eno’s synthesizer and sent back out transformed.
